summary: This video excerpt walks through a complex Photoshop workflow for manually blending two disparate landscape frames to create a seamless glacier/scan-style scene with flare management. The presenter emphasizes that perfect alignment is unattainable in manual blending, so the process relies on geometric warping (perspective and trapezoid shaping) to bring elements into a comparable frame, followed by careful painting with a hard-edge brush to hide misalignments. The workflow covers color matching (saturation, luminance, hue shifts), selective sky choices, and compositing of a single, cohesive sky. It also demonstrates a multi-zone approach to tonal adjustments, the use of Camera Raw and selective color for color grading, and finishing touches such as mid-tone dodge for water luminosity, a Vaseline-like vignette, and a guided crop to a 2:3 aspect. Throughout, the emphasis is on iterative, zone-based edits, re-timing adjustments, and the role of subjective aesthetic decisions when merging incompatible source imagery.

sections.title: Why Manual Blending Is So Hard
sections.description: Introduces the challenge of manually blending two very different landscape frames and explains why the images must be brought close to alignment before painting.

sections.title: Match Color and Prepare the Geometry
sections.description: Uses color adjustments to bring the two shots closer together visually, then evaluates the geometry needed to make the frames workable for blending.

sections.title: Warp the Left Side into a Trapezoid
sections.description: Applies perspective warping and trapezoidal shaping to stretch the left side of the frame so the horizon and foreground relationships can align better between images.

sections.title: Blend the Seam with a Hard-Edge Brush
sections.description: Paints across the overlap using hard edges and brush-size changes to hide the seam and make the two source shots read as one continuous scene.

sections.title: Choose a Sky and Rough in the Replacement
sections.description: Selects the better sky source, begins blending it into the composite, and trims the composition down to focus on the strongest portion of the scene.

sections.title: Crop Back to a Normal Composition
sections.description: Repositions the wide panorama into a more conventional two-by-three frame and rewarps the image to keep the water and horizon relationships stable.

sections.title: Work the Scene in Tonal Zones
sections.description: Breaks the image into tonal zones and explains the iterative workflow of adjusting one zone, then revisiting it after neighboring areas are refined.

sections.title: Camera Raw Corrections and Color Cleanup
sections.description: Uses Camera Raw to lower exposure, expand dynamic range, cool the color temperature, and remove unwanted green contamination from the rocks and midground.

sections.title: Rebuild Color with Selective Color and Lasso Masks
sections.description: Rebuilds color selectively for the highlights and sun-star area, then uses lasso-based masking and history-brush painting to control where the warmer color lands.

sections.title: Restore Greens and Dodge the Water
sections.description: Adds back a green cast to tree areas for depth and uses mid-tone dodge to brighten water and emphasize splash detail without disturbing the rest of the composite.

sections.title: Darken and Refine the Sky Blend
sections.description: Tones down the sky, adjusts its color balance, and blends it carefully into the scene while protecting the bright horizon line and nearby landscape.

sections.title: Add a Vaseline-Style Vignette
sections.description: Creates a custom vignette by darkening and cooling the edges, then painting the original image back in with history brush work to concentrate attention toward the center.

sections.title: Finish with Selective Blur and Glow
sections.description: Paints a brighter blurred version into selected areas to increase perceived depth and glow, especially around the center and sunlit regions.

sections.title: Wrap-Up and Key Takeaways
sections.description: Summarizes the main lessons: expose for the sky and sun star, warp and hand-blend incompatible frames, work by zones, and rebuild color tonally when the sources differ too much.
